PROJECT ODD PRICE

Tayabas Western Academy
Interactive Web-Based Retail Pricing Guide • Research Prototype

Research-based pricing guidance, made accessible

PROJECT ODD PRICE translates the study on odd-pricing strategies, processing fluency, and purchasing decision among BSBA students of Tayabas Western Academy into a practical digital decision-support guide.

ODD-PRICING

Review price endings

Compare nearby round and just-below price formats while keeping business costs and customer value in view.

PROCESSING FLUENCY

Improve price clarity

Assess readability, consistency, transparency, and ease of price comparison.

PURCHASE DECISION

Support informed evaluation

Use the guide to review price presentation without treating any price format as a guaranteed purchase trigger.

Suggested flow: Price Lab → Display Check → Retail Guide → Monitoring. The website is a guide, not a sales-prediction system.

Odd-Price Lab

Generate nearby price-format examples for comparison. Final prices should still consider cost, value, competition, and business context.

Enter product details to begin.

Price Display Check

Review whether a price presentation is easy to read, compare, and understand.

Clarity score: 0/6

Retail Pricing Guide

A simple application pathway derived from the study variables and recommendations.

1

Establish the regular price

Review product cost, desired return, customer budget, product value, and comparable market prices.

2

Compare price formats

Use the Price Lab to inspect a round reference and nearby just-below price examples.

3

Check processing fluency

Keep the displayed price readable, consistent, uncluttered, transparent, and easy to compare.

4

Apply responsibly

Select a price only when it remains supported by cost and value considerations. Avoid presenting price information in a misleading way.

5

Monitor and review

Record the price used, clarity assessment, and observations, then revise the presentation when needed.

Simple Monitoring Tool

Use this form to create a local review note for a product. Entries remain only on the current page session and are not uploaded anywhere.

About PROJECT ODD PRICE

Purpose

To translate findings on odd-pricing strategies, processing fluency, and purchasing decision into an accessible retail pricing guide.

Intended users

Local retailers, small business owners, student entrepreneurs, marketing students, and users reviewing retail price presentations.

Academic context

Developed as a research prototype associated with Tayabas Western Academy. The academy name and supplied academy logo are displayed for project identification.

Limitation: PROJECT ODD PRICE provides decision support only. It does not calculate complete profitability, predict sales, or guarantee purchasing behavior.
